ideas.resurrection_trigger: Complete 100 staged and 30 live cases with zero semantic overclaims, at least 30% faster resolution than a plain video call, and one installer or support provider committing to embed and pay.

ideas.name: ClapCut
ideas.one_liner: Use an explicit clap contract during app-owned recording to turn one long talking-head session into candidate take clips.
ideas.decision_reason: The detector is feasible, but the clap contaminates audio, interrupts performance, misfires on music and room noise, requires replacing Camera, and remains a thin feature beside mature cleanup editors. Tapping stop and start is a strong free substitute.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Across 300 intended boundaries require 98% recall, no more than one false split per hour, sub-15-second median cleanup, ten creators using it as primary recorder for ten sessions, and five $7.99 prepays.

ideas.name: LogoClock
ideas.one_liner: Find candidate time ranges where a creator-supplied sponsor logo appears and total the observed template exposure.
ideas.decision_reason: SponsorIQ and Shikenso already measure brand exposure, while sponsors usually care about spoken integration, prominence, context, performance, and contractual meaning rather than template seconds alone. Robust partial, rotated, animated, or occluded logo detection exceeds the simple phone wedge.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Five real briefs must specify logo-duration obligations, four of 15 creators must prepay, and a bounded nominated-template detector must exceed 95% precision and recall.

ideas.name: FocusReceipt
ideas.one_liner: Journal focus, exposure, white-balance, lens, and dropped-sample state changes during app-owned recording and show their timestamps afterward.
ideas.decision_reason: Mature cameras already expose locks and monitors that prevent the failure, and a third party cannot recover native Camera state after the fact. The observable journal is a recorder feature and cannot establish that a state change visibly ruined the take.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Ten of 20 phone filmmakers report monthly auto-mode losses this would change, four prepay, and the log agrees with visible fixture changes at least 90% of the time.

ideas.name: BumpMark
ideas.one_liner: Journal device attitude during a static app-owned shot and mark timestamps where the phone rotates beyond a threshold.
ideas.decision_reason: Core Motion can observe phone rotation, but stabilization may hide the visual effect and the user must replace a mature camera app. It discovers a possible issue after the fact and is more naturally a recorder feature than a standalone paid product.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Four of 15 high-frequency static-shot creators prepay and real markers save at least ten minutes weekly without implying a ruined shot.

ideas.name: CableWiggle
ideas.one_liner: Film a known low-voltage cable bundle while moving one cable from the far end and highlight the highest-motion candidate.
ideas.decision_reason: Adjacent cables move together, unknown or energized wiring can make the ritual inappropriate, and a low-cost toner/probe is authoritative. Optical flow can only identify observed motion, not continuity or identity.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Achieve at least 90% top-two accuracy across 100 bundled-cable trials and collect three of 12 professional prepays despite hardware testers.

ideas.name: CutReceipt
ideas.one_liner: Let a physically present client watch two exact video versions, choose one, and sign a byte-bound selection receipt on the vendor's phone.
ideas.decision_reason: RevCue, Frame.io, Vimeo Review, and Wipster already own video review and approval, while most clients are remote and need asynchronous comments. A signature cannot prove careful review or contract enforceability.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A counter-service vertical where clients are naturally present must produce at least five of 15 vendor prepays despite current review tools.

ideas.name: LoopSeam Lab
ideas.one_liner: Find endpoint candidates, preview repeated playback, and quantify frame and audio discontinuity for a short loop.
ideas.decision_reason: Mature loop editors already offer seam-related creation features. Pixel and audio similarity do not establish aesthetic continuity, and social platforms can alter playback after the local preview.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A reproducible platform-specific loop failure current editors miss plus eight of 12 repeat loop creators prepaying for that exact check.

ideas.name: CycleMatch
ideas.one_liner: Synchronize before-and-after equipment clips on a selected event and show observed motion-duration differences.
ideas.decision_reason: Generic synchronized comparison apps already provide side-by-side and overlay playback. Appearance, sound, and duration changes cannot diagnose repair correctness, so vertical positioning adds liability without a new invariant.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: One vertical supplies a standardized event with externally meaningful timing and repeat users prepay for the bounded comparison.

ideas.name: DualFormat Safety Capture
ideas.one_liner: Record one take into independently framed vertical and horizontal deliverable files.
ideas.decision_reason: DualShot Recorder, TwoFace, and a fast-growing 2026 clone swarm already sell the exact capture promise at $6.99–$9.99. The price proves focused camera-utility willingness to pay, not remaining whitespace.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A new hardware capability creates a genuinely different pair of outputs rather than another lens or orientation combination.

ideas.name: CeremonySafe
ideas.one_liner: Pair two phones to record independent local files for an irreplaceable event while showing connectivity and post-stop reopen state.
ideas.decision_reason: Final Cut Camera and Blackmagic already coordinate multiple phones, while obtaining, mounting, powering, pairing, and correctly aiming a second device is the dominant ritual. Software cannot ensure either view remains useful.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: An event partner plus 30 real ceremonies show easier completed setup and actual recovery versus the free tools.

ideas.name: RevisionReceipt
ideas.one_liner: Compare V1 and V2, bind objective change candidates and hashes to the exact V2 bytes, and collect client acknowledgment.
ideas.decision_reason: Video Compare App, Dropbox Replay, Frame.io, and similar systems own synchronized comparison, versions, comments, and approvals. A local receipt is too thin, while the complete useful version becomes another hosted review network.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Ten freelancers lose money specifically because existing review links lack a required byte-bound acknowledgment and prepay for that distinction.

ideas.name: ScreenSafe Recorder
ideas.one_liner: Mask or review sensitive pixels before sharing a mobile screen tutorial or bug recording.
ideas.decision_reason: Maskd already sells live Android protection, while iOS lacks equivalent sanctioned arbitrary cross-app window semantics. Post-capture OCR repeats false-negative risk over thousands of frames and cannot justify a safe claim.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Apple exposes sanctioned window and notification metadata, or paid users accept a mandatory full-review assistant that never claims the recording is safe.

ideas.name: Authentic OneTake
ideas.one_liner: Capture a no-cut app-owned video and attach signed C2PA Content Credentials for inspectable provenance.
ideas.decision_reason: Adobe, Sony, and C2PA already own the provenance standard, which explicitly cannot prove the depicted event is true. A self-signed consumer capture has weak value without hardware trust and downstream platform acceptance, and social transcoding can discard credentials.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A named publisher accepts the credential, a hardware-backed trust path exists, and a paid creator cohort receives concrete downstream value.

ideas.name: AppPreview Gate
ideas.one_liner: Check an App Store preview's length, dimensions, size, codec, frame rate, and audio against published rules.
ideas.decision_reason: StoreCut, Screeny, and a current tool swarm already create and validate previews against Apple's public specifications. Only App Store Connect decides acceptance, and the remaining creative rules are interpretive.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Apple introduces a new video asset class current tools cannot create or validate and the product reaches it before the swarm.

ideas.name: SoloMatch Voice
ideas.one_liner: Compare a solo creator's live framing with a saved reference and speak simple alignment cues before app-owned capture.
ideas.decision_reason: MatchFrame, ghost-overlay cameras, SoloSnap, Shootsolo, and Apple Watch Camera Remote already provide the component behaviors. Spoken corrections may be slower than a watch or overlay, and the active 2026 swarm can copy the refinement quickly.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Fifteen repeat-format creators use voice alignment for 80% of sessions over four weeks, ten prefer it to overlays or Watch, and eight prepay.

ideas.name: KeeperBuffer
ideas.one_liner: Keep a rolling app-owned camera buffer and save only the preceding interval after an unexpected great moment.
ideas.decision_reason: TapReplay already provides the exact free 5–60-second local buffer with screen, Bluetooth, and Watch triggers, while UpTakes, Loopr, Sideline Save, and sports replay tools crowd the behavior. The camera must already be open, aimed, powered, and hot before the unpredictable event.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A niche distribution partner demonstrates a workflow free TapReplay cannot serve and delivers a cohort willing to prepay.

ideas.name: BriefCut Gate
ideas.one_liner: Compare a sponsored-content brief with a final clip and surface bounded timestamped phrase, disclosure, duration, and visual-rule findings.
ideas.decision_reason: Vibe Analytics Brief Analyzer already performs brief parsing, timecodes, disclosure checks, mention counts, and rule reports, while semantic false negatives create dangerous compliance confidence. The natural payer is a brand or agency already served by B2B tools.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A creator-side objective rule current brief analyzers cannot serve, with no compliant green state and paid creator demand.

ideas.name: Match Relay
ideas.one_liner: Build a group film where each short clip must hand motion, shape, or sound to the next participant.
ideas.decision_reason: Reveal owns the group baton and hidden montage, MatchFrames owns visual alignment, and one missing or inaccurate participant breaks the artifact. The precision constraint adds friction without solving group-video cold start.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Twenty manual relays achieve 70% invite-to-clip conversion, 60% four-link completion, 50% second-relay creation, and five $7.99 host prepays.

ideas.name: Hidden Group Video Drop
ideas.one_liner: Collect private friend clips that remain hidden until a deadline reveals the group montage.
ideas.decision_reason: Reveal and Auree now own the exact hidden-until-reveal collaborative capture and host-paid event flow, including no-install contribution paths.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A named audience demonstrates and prepays for a response contract neither exact product supports.

ideas.name: Video Challenge League
ideas.one_liner: Run prompted one-take video challenges with public voting, rankings, and winners.
ideas.decision_reason: Clippoll, Aura, Top That, Trendoline, Youzem, and related 2026 products form an exact swarm around prompts, duels, voting, prizes, and leaderboards.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A genuinely different atomic response rule and seed community produce paid repeat behavior before a network build.

ideas.name: Friend Video Elimination
ideas.one_liner: Run a private friend-group video-dare season where deadlines and votes eliminate players to a final winner.
ideas.decision_reason: Captains launched the exact format with private groups, captain rotation, deadlines, eliminations, final voting, archive, comments, and chat.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: The exact incumbent disappears or a funded community partner requires a rule Captains cannot support.

ideas.name: Multi-Angle Moment
ideas.one_liner: Collect attendee clips and switch among cameras at the same event timestamp during playback.
ideas.decision_reason: Relive and Recap already own synchronized multi-POV event playback. Clock drift, duplicate coverage, mixed orientation, music, minors, permissions, and storage add operational cost without a fresh format.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A venue or event partner supplies timing, rights, distribution, and prepaid demand for a missing interaction.

ideas.name: Shared Day Episode
ideas.one_liner: Collect tiny clips from a group and turn a day, trip, or month into a finite shared episode.
ideas.decision_reason: 1 Second Everyday, Leap Second, Dotty, and Sway already combine daily capture, collaboration, split-screen, trips, and recap outputs with mature paid behavior.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A new output contract proves repeat creation and payment beyond the established collaborative recap tools.

ideas.name: Reaction Escrow
ideas.one_liner: Record a consenting recipient's face while viewing a clip and reveal the paired reaction afterward.
ideas.decision_reason: Slice, Seen, Real Reaction, and Reacts already occupy reaction recording and chains, while coercion, copyrighted source capture, self-consciousness, and accidental recording of private surroundings create structural trust risk.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Users request the mechanic inside a bounded, rights-cleared coaching vertical with explicit pre-record consent and payment.

ideas.name: Video Postcards
ideas.one_liner: Send private face-to-face video updates that close relationships watch and answer asynchronously.
ideas.decision_reason: Marco Polo owns the behavior with mature monthly, annual, and family subscriptions. The market validates private video willingness to pay but leaves no new atomic loop.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A narrow relationship or accessibility contract current asynchronous video messengers cannot serve and users prepay for it.

ideas.name: What Happens Next Video
ideas.one_liner: Watch a video setup, commit to an ending, and reveal the real clip as a daily puzzle.
ideas.decision_reason: An exact 2026 App Store product and similar Android products already own the format, while licensed, staged, or scraped content supply remains the business and weak payment signal.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A rights-cleared content partner plus demonstrated paid daily retention unavailable to current products.

ideas.name: Video Scavenger Story
ideas.one_liner: Issue video missions during a party, trip, or city outing and assemble completed clips into a recap story.
ideas.decision_reason: Scavos, Eventzee, Goosechase, SnapQuest, and related products already sell photo/video missions and party packs. The exact willingness to pay exists, but the format is occupied.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A new mission-to-output contract current scavenger products cannot reproduce and event hosts prepay for it.

ideas.name: Remix Response Contract
ideas.one_liner: Let a creator declare a structured harmony, motion, shot, or answer slot and collect attributed video responses.
ideas.decision_reason: TikTok and YouTube already own Duet, Stitch, Collab, Cut, Add Yours, templates, attribution, distribution, and music rights. Source deletion or revoked remix permissions can also mute or remove downstream work.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A rights-owning creator community commits distribution and payment for a response rule the major platforms cannot express.

ideas.name: Actor Scene Test
ideas.one_liner: Record a short provided scene, compare takes with a professional reference, and join recurring role challenges.
ideas.decision_reason: Dr Self Tape, Rehearsed, Cue Line, and Slatable already serve actor practice, self-tape recording, readers, comparison, feedback, and scene challenges. Script rights and appearance-based peer judgment add risk.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A training partner supplies licensed scenes and a paid interaction current actor utilities cannot add cheaply.

ideas.name: FrameFault
ideas.one_liner: Decode a selected final video locally and shortlist near-black spans or one-to-five-frame visual outliers for human review.
ideas.decision_reason: Auto QC, UploadCheck, and QC Buddy now detect black or frozen frames, silence, integrity, and delivery-spec failures with generous free tiers. Intentional flashes, cuts, and black beats create false positives, while full 4K and HDR decode is slow and hot on a phone.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Five of 20 editors explicitly refuse cloud upload and prepay, scans run faster than half real time on target devices, and false flags remain below one per minute.

ideas.name: BackPocket.help
ideas.one_liner: An AI front office scopes a small real-world problem, finds a safe next move, and hands a prepared bounded job to a local human finisher.
ideas.decision_reason: A live synthetic prototype demonstrates the AI-operated, human-finished service loop and a concrete $69 rescue offer, but it has not yet shown an unaffiliated paid customer, repeatable fulfillment, safe triage accuracy, or sustainable unit economics.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Advance only after at least three unaffiliated customers pay for supported jobs, every job stays inside the published safety boundary, agent logs show the production decisions, and contribution margin remains positive after human labor, travel, support, refunds, and model cost.

ideas.name: Did-It-Fix-It
ideas.one_liner: Link a vehicle complaint, the repair invoice, and bounded later owner observations so the next shop can see whether the original symptom returned.
ideas.decision_reason: Service records preserve transactions better than outcomes, but AutoVitals already branches follow-up on unresolved symptoms and CARFAX or shop suites can absorb the feature. Consumer use is episodic, outcomes are self-reported, and the paying shop owns retention.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Reopen only with shop or insurer distribution, repeated follow-up adherence, evidence the packet materially changes a later visit, and paying multi-vehicle users despite current shop-side follow-up.

ideas.name: Change Impact Relay
ideas.one_liner: When a child or family schedule changes, show which declared rides and commitments it breaks and send the right adult a no-install reassignment link.
ideas.decision_reason: Caldzy, Aviva, Ohai, PlanPing, and family calendars already occupy schedule conflict and coordination. A maintained dependency graph is a new ritual, and an incomplete graph can create false calm about rides, care, work, or gear consequences.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Reopen only if 100 real changes expose at least 30 missed consequences, setup stays under two minutes, at least 70% of no-app reassignment links receive an unprompted response, and five users prepay despite the incumbent swarm.

ideas.name: Client Decision Debt Clock
ideas.one_liner: Give a client one bounded choice with a deadline and show exactly how their delay moves the freelancer's delivery date.
ideas.decision_reason: ApproveEase already offers the same no-login magic link, reminders, and automatic delivery-date movement, while approval and project platforms own the surrounding workflow. Software also cannot create client leverage by itself.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Reopen only if the exact incumbent leaves a material gap or a vertical distribution channel beats ordinary email and current approval tools with at least five prepays.

ideas.name: Repair Relay
ideas.one_liner: Preserve a wheelchair or assistive-device repair timeline and route a factual escalation packet through a sanctioned clinic, vendor, or advocacy path.
ideas.decision_reason: The pain is severe, but the phone does not own provider status and a manual diary cannot become repair truth. The concept is unsafe and weak without a sanctioned escalation partner.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A wheelchair clinic, repair vendor, payer, or advocacy organization agrees to a sanctioned status and escalation pilot with compensated disabled-user co-design.

ideas.name: Departure Baton
ideas.one_liner: Assign the last safety-critical RV departure checks between partners and preserve who acknowledged each bounded step.
ideas.decision_reason: The handoff is real and phone-friendly, but acknowledgment does not prove physical completion and a laminated checklist may be faster, safer, and more reliable.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Run a five-pair paper-versus-phone test; advance only if the phone is faster, produces fewer unowned steps, and never presents acknowledgment as physical verification.

ideas.name: Used Gear Passport
ideas.one_liner: Carry source-linked service and ownership records with a high-value used item when a trusted repair shop, dealer, or marketplace seeds them.
ideas.decision_reason: The record could reduce secondhand uncertainty, but consumer-entered history is not authoritative and a two-sided trust network has fatal cold start without an industry distribution partner.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: One repair shop, dealer, or enthusiast marketplace agrees to seed verifiable records and distribute the passport in a narrow high-value category.

ideas.name: 311 Shadow Receipt
ideas.one_liner: Preserve a resident-owned history of one city's 311 requests and compare official status changes with the source events the city API exposes.
ideas.decision_reason: A factual shadow history may reveal missing records or status/outcome mismatches, but the city remains authoritative, consumer willingness to pay is weak, and usefulness depends on one sanctioned live API and trusted distribution.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A neighborhood or accessibility organization sponsors a one-city pilot whose live API supports the history; success requires recovered missing source history or documented official status/outcome mismatches.

ideas.name: Monetization Canary
ideas.one_liner: Record factual paywall and purchase-path health by build and storefront, then alert when an offering is empty, price data is absent, or a purchase terminates in an error.
ideas.decision_reason: The runtime boundary is observable and recurring, but RevenueCat already owns diagnostic telemetry and paywall callbacks while Sentry or PostHog can capture custom failures. A separate probe is a vertical preset with integration burden and extreme host-feature absorption risk.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: First confirm RevenueCat has no equivalent imminent alert, then require at least five of 15 indie developers to install a test probe, three to make a credible paid commitment, and half to submit a second release trace within 30 days; kill if ordinary observability reproduces the diagnosis in under 15 minutes for most testers.

ideas.name: SnapInvoice
ideas.one_liner: Turn a solo tradesperson's week of job photos and paper slips into sendable invoice lines and flag any job that never got billed.
ideas.decision_reason: Survived full MCLOVIN round 12 as the strongest Shipaton candidate, but the post-commit live audit materially lowered novelty. SimplyWise combines photo-to-line-item estimates with invoicing, while BldrOS, PeakPro, PlanMyCrew, SodaDesk, and TidyShift market adjacent photo-backed billing or completed-but-unbilled detection. No exact standalone product was found for the remaining behavior wedge: forward existing job photos or slips without adopting a field-service suite, draft invoice lines, and flag the job until an invoice is sent. Business payer and weekly retention remain plausible. Not BUILD: first prove operators reject the suites but prepay for this narrower intake, then prove line-extraction accuracy and repeated forwarding behavior.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Advance only if >=7 of 10 eligible ops demonstrate why current suites fail their workflow, >=4 place a refundable deposit for the narrower service, a fixture proves >=90% extractable line-item accuracy with no false green on unreadable slips, >=7 of 10 use it on >=80% of real jobs, and >=4 convert to a paid founder offer.

ideas.name: ReturnShield
ideas.one_liner: Photograph and document returned items at intake and package dispute-ready evidence so online resellers stop losing refunds they could have defended.
ideas.decision_reason: Second strongest Shipaton candidate. Return fraud is $103B/yr with 15.14% of returns fraudulent (NRF/LP Media); resellers already photograph returns as self-protection; the micro-reseller evidence workflow has no dedicated tool (Loop Returns serves mid-market; novelty ~55). Business/prosumer payer, retention per return. Not BUILD: reseller willingness-to-pay and marketplace-adjudication limits are unproven.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: 20 active resellers prepay after evidence packs measurably improve dispute outcomes; retention above two returns per week.

ideas.name: NetCheck
ideas.one_liner: Compare a gig worker's 1099-K gross, platform statements, and bank deposits to show actual taxable income by platform and flag gross-vs-deposits mismatches.
ideas.decision_reason: Highest-novelty survivor of round 12 (no direct product found, novelty ~70) but wrong timing for Shipaton (tax season is not inside the 6-week window), weak phone advantage (document-heavy), seasonal retention, and the Ledger's recurring two-record-invariant risk. Related to the existing gig-payout-deposit-match and etsy-payout-reconciliation records.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Tax-season demand window (Jan-Apr), evidence gig workers pay year-round for deduction prep, or a stable invariant demonstrated on real platform statements.

ideas.name: ShipKit
ideas.one_liner: Camera-based measurement, freight-class lookup, live large-item shipping quotes, and a claim-proof packaging workflow for resellers.
ideas.decision_reason: Real reseller pain (large-item shipping costs kill deals; armchair $385-515 vs $95-210 via uShip) but the product composes existing parts (uShip rails, FreightSizer camera-to-freight-class); the bundle plus a mandatory damage-photo workflow needs proof of retention (novelty ~50).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Resellers demonstrate weekly retention and prepay; evidence the bundle beats the uShip/FreightSizer components separately.

ideas.name: PaywallDoc
ideas.one_liner: Reads an indie developer's RevenueCat paywall, store listing, and review themes and emits one ranked monetization hypothesis with a concrete change per week.
ideas.decision_reason: HAMM-dogfood angle is real (Shipaton's own audience of 15,202 devs; sanctioned RevenueCat data gives the product owned state) but novelty is thin (Superwall AI, app-paywall-pilot GitHub; novelty ~30), the phone surface is weak (a web/desktop job), and RevenueCat could ship the digest as a feature.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence indie devs pay for weekly monetization guidance that RevenueCat does not ship; a mobile-first surface proves retention.

ideas.name: RVWatchdog
ideas.one_liner: An RV owner photographs mileage and location at shop dropoff; the app tracks days-in-shop and generates escalation nudges to the dealer and manufacturer warranty lines.
ideas.decision_reason: The only shop-agnostic owner-side watchdog found (novelty ~55), but RV repairs are low-frequency (34-day average cycle; no retention), the 'industry average days-in-shop' benchmark data does not exist (false-certainty trap), and shops are hostile to owner-side tooling (host-owns-correction).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence RV owners act on escalation within a week of a stalled repair, or a sanctioned shop API; frequency above quarterly.

ideas.name: MailForward Forensics
ideas.one_liner: Photograph forwarded USPS mail during a move to OCR the sender and generate the 'you forgot to update X' list with direct update links.
ideas.decision_reason: Novel (no direct product found, novelty ~75), phone-native, and attaches to the sanctioned USPS forwarding signal as the trigger - but low frequency and consumers won't pay for a checklist, and the update step has no sanctioned API (aggregator-without-API trap).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence movers pay; a sanctioned way to trigger the updates; bundling with a higher-frequency moving product.

ideas.name: Photo-to-Quote Instant Estimator
ideas.one_liner: A customer sends a photo of a repair problem and a tradesperson dictates; a branded estimate exits in under a minute.
ideas.decision_reason: DIRECT to SimplyWise Cost Estimator (4.8 stars, ~31k ratings, 10k+ contractors) plus FieldQuote and Billio; the photo-to-branded-estimate-to-PDF job is occupied at scale (novelty ~15). Only inbound-text and dictate-only slivers are open, and the suites can ship them.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: SimplyWise/FieldQuote exit, or an inbound channel they do not serve (WhatsApp/WeChat) shows real adoption.

ideas.name: Proofing Catalog Seam
ideas.one_liner: Sync client gallery selections, comments, and retouch scribbles back into Lightroom Classic or Capture One.
ideas.decision_reason: Gallerina occupies the Lightroom return-path; Pic-Time sync and Proofr overlap; Adobe has a native feature request pending (platform risk). The Capture One wedge is open but small and is a feature, not a moat (novelty ~20).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Adobe ships no native return-path and photographers demonstrate they pay for a third-party seam; Capture One share grows.

ideas.name: No-Account Client Galleries
ideas.one_liner: Mobile-first, link-only photo galleries with graceful full-res download and per-recipient audit, without print-shop bloat.
ideas.decision_reason: Picflow owns the no-account link-only gallery; Framekeep and SendPhoto overlap; native substitutes (Apple/Google Photos) and consumer-won't-pay churn (novelty ~10).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A proofing niche Picflow ignores shows willingness to pay.

ideas.name: Owner-Owned Repair Record
ideas.one_liner: An owner-owned, portable, exportable service record for a car with part before/after photos and receipts.
ideas.decision_reason: Odobook literally markets 'portable copy of service history, free CSV export'; CARFAX Car Care is the free incumbent (4.84 stars, 125k ratings); consumer-won't-pay; connected-car native substitute (novelty ~5).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Resale/dealership demand makes portability a paid event; a dealer-pays integration.

ideas.name: Repair Shop Status Timeline
ideas.one_liner: A repair shop publishes greet-to-estimate-approved-to-parts-inbound-to-done status with photo proof per step.
ideas.decision_reason: TrueStatus does exactly this (tracking code at dropoff plus real-time photo updates per step); Tekmetric/Shop-Ware/Fullbay/Jobber bundle customer portals; host-owns-correction - the shop controls the channel (novelty ~10).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Shops prove they adopt an owner-side neutral channel; shop-owned-state changes.

ideas.name: Handoff Evidence Camera
ideas.one_liner: Geo-timestamped condition capture at every transfer point (owner-to-shop, buyer-to-seller, tenant-to-landlord) for dispute-ready timelines.
ideas.decision_reason: Commodity timestamp/geostamp cameras plus vertical incumbents (SnapProof, MeInspect, StayProof, InspectYour); a horizontal 'every transfer point' is a wrapper; the phone camera already geotags (novelty ~20).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A vertical with a sanctioned API and a payer (a business that mandates the record) emerges.

ideas.name: Paystub-Schedule Diff
ideas.one_liner: Photo the posted schedule and the paystub; compute hours worked versus hours paid and flag mismatches for hourly workers.
ideas.decision_reason: WageWatch App (2025, labor-lawyer-built) does exactly this; duplicates the existing timecard-paystub-pair record's job; hourly workers won't pay; employer-hosted correction (novelty ~25).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Labor-org or union distribution channel pays; employer-side adoption.

ideas.name: Move-In Condition Report
ideas.one_liner: A timed room-by-room move-in walkthrough video with damage tags, stored with lease metadata, exported as a condition report.
ideas.decision_reason: DepositProof, MoveProof, door.lease, and Walk Thru all launched within 18 months (crowding); links to the existing security-deposit-evidence record; tenant-side monetization unproven (novelty ~10).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Landlord/PM mandates the record (B2B), or a state statute creates a standardized deposit process.

ideas.name: Deposit-Recovery Packet
ideas.one_liner: At move-out, generate an itemized deposit dispute packet with comparison clips and a state-law deadline cheat sheet.
ideas.decision_reason: DepositGenie and DepositsBack occupy the tenant-side dispute niche; links to the existing security-deposit-evidence record; one-shot cadence (novelty ~10).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A state regulatory change standardizing deposits creates a compliance-payer.

ideas.name: Executor Death-Admin Ledger
ideas.one_liner: A US 'Tell Us Once': an executor's ledger to notify organizations, track document scans, deadlines, and probate to-dos after a death.
ideas.decision_reason: Empathy.com and EstateExec occupy the executor workflow; Everplans was sold and Lantern shut down (graveyard); one-shot usage kills retention and subscription; morbid acquisition is expensive (novelty ~10).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Funeral-home or estate-attorney B2B distribution with a recurring channel; a state digital-death law.

ideas.name: Credential Wall for Small Employers
ideas.one_liner: A shared staff-license tracker with scheduled official-lookup re-checks and audit-ready exports for small employers.
ideas.decision_reason: Certemy provides the exact feature set; the spreadsheet crowd has low audit risk; boards and CE Broker own the data and already email renewals (native substitute; novelty ~12).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A regulated-industry shift forces small employers to audit; licensing boards open sanctioned APIs.

ideas.name: License Renewal Watch
ideas.one_liner: Photo a professional license; the app re-checks the board's public lookup and alerts on status drops or renewal windows.
ideas.decision_reason: Nursys e-Notify is free and official for nurses; board lookups are fragmented and captcha'd (no sanctioned API); a 2026 wave of 0-rating tracker apps shows no individual willingness to pay (novelty ~5-35).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Multi-state contractors with no board email coverage prove willingness to pay; a sanctioned board API.

ideas.name: DMV-Passport Slot Alerter
ideas.one_liner: Watch a DMV or passport-portal appointment calendar and push when a slot opens.
ideas.decision_reason: DMV NC Appointment (2021), Visa Appointment Alerts (2026), and ~15 OSS bots; no dominant multi-agency product but the job is trivial to clone; low frequency, one-shot value (novelty ~20).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A high-stakes portal (e.g., visa) with an official API and proof users will pay for priority slots.

ideas.name: Traveler Incident Workspace
ideas.one_liner: A traveler's screenshot-append evidence pack with a receipt trail, family status page, and entitlement reference during a travel disruption.
ideas.decision_reason: FlightRights (2026), RefundMe AI, and AirHelp occupy the entitlement/claims layer; airlines auto-rebook and own the truth (host-owns-correction); disruption is episodic (retention; novelty ~30).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A regulation (e.g., a US EU-style passenger-rights rule) creates a claims window with a consumer payer; a sanctioned airline status API.

ideas.name: Accessibility Report Card
ideas.one_liner: Turn a professional accessibility audit into a shareable consumer-facing score for a business.
ideas.decision_reason: Liability magnet - AccessiBe was fined $1M by the FTC and UserWay was sued; host-audits-own-score makes the rating defensible; monetization is specialist-side and not a 6-week consumer app (novelty ~40 but hostile).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A standards body owns the score (e.g., W3C), removing liability; a specialist-pays distribution channel.

ideas.name: Easy-Cancel Subscription Intake
ideas.one_liner: Compliant sign-up for small subscription businesses with pre-wired easy cancel to reduce chargebacks.
ideas.decision_reason: Stripe Billing Customer Portal, Recurly, and Chargebee already own the cancel UX; the FTC click-to-cancel rule was vacated (Jul 2025), removing the regulatory tailwind; selling to merchants in 6 weeks is slow (novelty ~30).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: The revived click-to-cancel rule creates a compliance-payer; merchants prove they buy standalone cancel UX.

ideas.name: Quote Follow-Up Nudger
ideas.one_liner: Tracks a pro's quotes that went silent and nudges the prospect or the pro before the job is lost.
ideas.decision_reason: Two-party cold start (pros must adopt); commodity CRM/reminder surface; no evidence pros will pay for follow-up automation (contractor no-show and silent quotes are a strong consumer pain, but the fixer is the pro, not the app).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A distribution channel where pros already aggregate (marketplace) and evidence they pay for follow-up.

ideas.name: Local Marketplace Auto-Reprice
ideas.one_liner: Airline-yield-style auto-reprice-to-deadline for local marketplace listings (Facebook/Craigslist).
ideas.decision_reason: Most novel mechanic found this round (novelty ~80) but structurally hostile: no sanctioned marketplace API, ToS bans automation, Meta's native seller tooling, and 7-day listing cycles.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A sanctioned marketplace API or a marketplace that permits repricing; evidence sellers pay.

ideas.name: Home Warranty Claim Forensics
ideas.one_liner: Guided photo and timebox capture during a home breakdown plus a checklist of what the denial letter will demand.
ideas.decision_reason: No direct product found (novelty ~60) but demand is thin: denials are usually coverage exclusions; claims are low-stakes and one-time; the warranty company owns the decision (host-owns-correction).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence warranty holders repeatedly appeal and pay for evidence; a warranty company partners.

ideas.name: NOTAM-Style Commute Digest
ideas.one_liner: Reformat dated road-closure and hazard bulletins into a daily commute-relevant digest.
ideas.decision_reason: Navigation apps (Google Maps/Waze) own real-time routing; reformatted alerts are a content play with no payer and native substitution.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A government feed that navigation apps do not consume (school closures, parade routes) with an engaged audience.

ideas.name: Aviation-MEL Deferred Repairs
ideas.one_liner: Aviation-style 'broken but tolerated with a hard deadline' log for deferred home and car repairs.
ideas.decision_reason: Interesting cross-domain mechanism (from aviation minimum-equipment-list practice) but low urgency for consumers and no clear payer; could pair with a repair product as a module.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A repair-verification product needs a deferred-items module.

ideas.name: Freight-Line Pro
ideas.one_liner: Camera measurement to freight class to live quote to claim-proof packaging, built as a weekly-volume margin tool for auction houses, estate liquidators, and furniture dealers.
ideas.decision_reason: Round 12 mechanism-transplant candidate: freight misclassification and DIM-weight surprises eat margin for businesses that ship multiple items weekly (auction houses, estate liquidators, furniture dealers). Unlike the parked reseller-focused ShipKit, this targets a business payer with weekly volume who owns the shipping step. Kept raw: the competitor check is incomplete (search engines bot-walled mid-pass, so the cell is 'unverified-occupied' not 'verified-empty'), and the mechanic is composed of existing parts (uShip/LTL rails, camera measurement).
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Five auction/estate-liquidation businesses prepay after a 20-shipment study shows measurable misclassification recoveries; a verified competitor sweep finds the phone-native photo-to-class-to-quote-to-claim cell open.

ideas.name: User-Instrumentable Process Tracker
ideas.one_liner: A user logs their own steps, documents, deadlines, and evidence across any multi-provider process; the app answers 'what happens next' from the user's own inputs plus calendar math, never the provider's state.
ideas.decision_reason: FALSIFIED in Round 12 despite the strongest pain convergence of Round 11 (7 independent research paths on 'what happens next'). The literal cell (consumer-owned, multi-provider, user-instrumented) is empty for economic reasons, not oversight: consumers pay only for actual provider status (Lawfully, 6M+ cases, proves this), episodic processes kill retention, and the shareable status-page mechanism is already commoditized from the business side at the price floor (TrueStatus, BuildStatus $15/mo, SiteUpdate, Jobber/Buildertrend). The contractor-side variant is a 2025-26 growth wave, not an open wedge.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence consumers pay for their OWN process record (not just actual status); a single-process vertical with a business payer that the TrueStatus/BuildStatus wave does not cover; or a state-change stream with a sanctioned API.

ideas.name: Done-Needs-Confirmation
ideas.one_liner: Sell the repair shop a verified-done transparency tool: tech photos plus customer sign-off that kills 'is it done?' calls and disputes — the host becomes the customer, escaping host-owns-correction.
ideas.decision_reason: Round 12 Weirdness-Round survivor and the round's most interesting mechanism (host-buys-transparency inversion). PARTIAL to CompanyCam (28,888 ratings) and Timemark 'Photo Proof for Work' (13,811 ratings); the standalone solo-shop customer-facing sign-off wedge is open but the buyer already pays for field-service suites, and the mechanism is cheap to copy.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: Evidence solo shops without a suite pay specifically for the customer-facing sign-off and verified-done proof; a shop-side channel with weekly use.

ideas.name: Claim-Ready Install Record
ideas.one_liner: Sell contractors a claim-ready install record (serial, date, photos, sign-off) built at origin so home-warranty 'no records' denials physically cannot be made.
ideas.decision_reason: Round 12 Weirdness-Round survivor: inverts the home-warranty evidence problem (FG01) by making the contractor the buyer of a portable claim file. Host-side absorption risk is real (Liberty Home Guard and AHS capture serial/model photos in their own apps); the vendor-neutral portable claim file is open but the buyer is fragmented and the incumbent warranty companies are the host.
ideas.resurrection_trigger: A home-warranty or manufacturer partner mandates the record (B2B channel); evidence contractors pay for a portable claim file that outlives their customer relationship.
